Subject: Post-call: Performance / SLO qualification — context window & latency impact

Hi Alex / Priya — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap + next steps so we’re all aligned.

Call summary (short):
- Goal: Productionize FinCo’s document-assistant flow for customer support — tight latency and streaming UX required.
- Typical request shape: ~1.2–1.8k input tokens (document + user prompt), expected output up to ~512 tokens; peak cases up to ~2k output tokens for long-form summaries.
- Key SLO asks discussed: p95 end-to-end latency target, sustained concurrency, and streaming behavior for progressive rendering in the web UI.

Specific asks I captured:
- Target p95 for interactive queries: < 750 ms (for the majority of queries)
- Peak concurrency: ~40 concurrent active users (bursty), sustained ~15–20
- Throughput: ~200–300 requests/hour per team, but spikes up to 1k/hr in peak windows
- Streaming required: yes — need partial tokens to render as they arrive for perceived latency
- Context window: evaluating 32k vs 8k; want to understand latency and cost tradeoffs when retaining full document context vs summarizing/cache approach

Proposed next steps from Redwood:
1) Technical deep-dive with your infra/engineering team to validate throughput and token distributions (can we do Wed/Thu next week?)
2) Share SLO calc sheet and perf profile for 8k vs 32k models (attached) — Rishi and Dev to review latency expectations and recommended config
3) Quick pilot runbook: 2-week test on Dedicated pool with streaming enabled + prefix caching to measure real-world p95.

Attached: FINCO_SLO_calc_sheet.xlsx (SLOs & assumptions), redwood_perf_profile_32k_ctx.pdf (latency profiles we’ve measured across context windows).

Ping me if any of the recapped points are off. If not, I’ll send proposed times for the deep dive.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Thanks Marissa — this looks right. Couple clarifications from our side:

1) Latency target nuance: the 750 ms p95 is for our primary short-response flow (user asks, assistant returns a short answer ~<128 tokens). For the long-form summarization path we can accept higher p95 (up to ~1.5s) but streaming is critical — users must see first tokens within ~250–350 ms.

2) Context window: most of our docs are long. Realistically, we’ll need to support up to 32k windows for the first phase; for historical threads we can fall back to summarized context. We want to understand the delta in per-token generation latency when moving from 8k -> 32k (and any nonlinear impacts).

3) Concurrency: our product load balancing is per-user; we expect short bursts where concurrency reaches ~40–50 for <5 minutes. Can Redwood autoscale fast enough to keep p95 within target during these bursts?

4) Security/PCI: Priya will follow up separately on logs retention and SOC-2 artifacts (looping procurement later).

Looking forward to the deep-dive — Alex

Thanks Alex — great clarifications. Short technical notes to set expectations before the deep-dive:

- Context window impact:
  - For generation, model compute is roughly proportional to generated tokens; however, attention and KV-cache management cause per-step overhead that increases with context length. In practice we observe:
    - 8k -> p95 generation latency baseline X (depends on model),
    - 32k -> additional overhead that can be ~1.2x–1.6x on per-token throughput for long inputs depending on model architecture and kernel selection. The nonlinear cost grows with both input length and the attention pattern (sparse vs dense).

- Streaming and first-token latency:
  - Streaming reduces perceived latency because the first tokens are delivered as soon as softmax resamples begin. For long outputs, sending the first chunk within 200–350 ms is achievable with properly tuned batching and small initial decode lengths (we usually stream 64–128 token chunks).

- Concurrency & autoscaling:
  - Recommended for your burst profile: Dedicated pool (reserved capacity) with headroom for burst autoscaling to handle 40–50 concurrent active requests. Suggested per-GPU concurrency config: 8–12 inferences (depending on model size), with aggressive horizontal autoscaling triggers at 70% GPU utilization. This keeps queueing low and p95 predictable.

- Practical options we recommend to meet your UX goals:
  1) Pilot on a 32k-capable model but use prefix-summarization/caching for historical docs to reduce average context length — minimizes latency and cost while keeping fidelity when required.
  2) Use streaming with small initial chunk sizes (64 tokens) to ensure first-token render <350 ms.
  3) Configure low batching (batch size 1–4) for latency-sensitive endpoints and allow a separate high-throughput path with larger batching for non-interactive jobs.
  4) If p95 for some critical short flows needs <500 ms strictly, consider pinning to a smaller context model (8k) for that route.

Attached is a filled SLO calc with conservative throughput and latency assumptions (FINCO_SLO_calc_sheet.xlsx) and our measured perf profile for 32k contexts (redwood_perf_profile_32k_ctx.pdf). Rishi / Dev — feel free to add any numbers I missed.

If that looks good I’ll send proposed slots for a technical deep-dive (30–45 minutes) and include our infra lead.

Best,
Marissa
